subsystems.name: Optical sensor module
subsystems.role: shines infrared and red light into the finger and measures the reflected light to derive heart rate and blood oxygen.

subsystems.name: Motion and temperature sensors
subsystems.role: track movement and skin temperature to help distinguish sleep stages and detect illness trends.

subsystems.name: Low-power electronics
subsystems.role: processes sensor data on the ring and manages power.

subsystems.name: Battery and charging
subsystems.role: stores enough energy for several days and recharges inductively.

subsystems.name: Wireless link
subsystems.role: syncs data to a phone app via Bluetooth Low Energy.

subsystems.name: Housing and materials
subsystems.role: protects the electronics, stays comfortable and waterproof.

buildSteps.title: Design the optical stack
buildSteps.detail: Engineer the placement and angles of LEDs and photodiodes so they get a clean pulse signal from the finger's arteries.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the flexible circuit
buildSteps.detail: Assemble sensors, microcontroller and radio on a small flexible printed circuit board that curves around the finger.

buildSteps.title: Make the ring shell
buildSteps.detail: Machine or mould the outer shell and prepare the inner cavity for electronics.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the electronics
buildSteps.detail: Place the battery, circuit board and sensor module inside the shell, connecting them and sealing with resin.

buildSteps.title: Finish and coat
buildSteps.detail: Cure the resin, polish the ring and apply a durable, skin-safe coating.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate sensors
buildSteps.detail: Individually calibrate each ring's optical and temperature sensors against known references.

buildSteps.title: Flash firmware and test
buildSteps.detail: Load algorithms for heart rate, HRV and sleep staging, then test wireless pairing, battery life and water resistance.

buildSteps.title: Quality control and packaging
buildSteps.detail: Check fit, finish and function, then package with a charging dock.

prerequisites.why: they measure blood volume changes optically, which is the basis for heart rate and oxygen saturation from a finger.

prerequisites.tech: Low-power microcontrollers and Bluetooth Low Energy
prerequisites.why: they allow days of battery life while processing and syncing continuous data.
they fit inside a ring and store enough energy for multi-day use.
they infer sleep stages from heart rate, HRV and movement, though accuracy varies compared with lab polysomnography.
they keep the device safe and comfortable for continuous wear, including in water.

pathway.milestone: consumer rings like the Oura Ring Gen3 track sleep, readiness and heart rate trends
pathway.unlocks: widespread personal awareness of sleep and recovery.

pathway.milestone: more sensors (e.g. continuous blood pressure or glucose) and better algorithms
pathway.unlocks: broader health monitoring from a finger.

pathway.milestone: regulatory clearances for specific medical alerts, such as irregular heart rhythm detection
pathway.unlocks: trusted use in clinical care and screening.

pathway.milestone: integration with electronic health records and remote patient monitoring
pathway.unlocks: continuous, passive monitoring for chronic conditions.
